Chapter Details: Comparable indicators on energy, connectivity and data storage. 27 variables in 5 sections. Contains latest available data. Data collection by Perplexity from a variety of sources.
Definition: The country's total international internet bandwidth capacity per internet user, indicating the quality and capacity of the country's connection to the global internet. Determined by submarine cable landings (for coastal states), cross-border terrestrial fibre (for landlocked states), and satellite links.
revision_notes: Cited source fetched and confirmed: TheGlobalEconomy.com reports ITU-sourced data of 4.00 kbit/s per internet user for Uganda in 2016 (data series covers 2012-2016 only), which correctly supports Value Code 1 (Very Low, <5 kbit/s per user). Searched ITU DataHub, World Bank IT.NET.BNDW.PC/IT.NET.BNDW metadata, TeleGeography State of the Network reports (2023/2024), and Uganda Communications Commission Annual Sector Report 2023 for a fresher country-level bandwidth-per-user figure; none publish an updated per-user kbit/s figure for Uganda, and the ITU indicator appears to have been discontinued in recent country reporting (no data after 2016 found). UCC data show substantial infrastructure growth since 2016 (national fibre network grew from 5,700km in 2013 to 30,161km in 2023; new submarine/terrestrial capacity including the Umoja cable has since reached the region), which suggests the true current figure is likely higher, but no authoritative source was found to support a specific higher code. Score confirmed on existing evidence only; flagged for human review given the decade-old vintage of the only available figure and the likelihood it understates current capacity.
revised_comments: The most recent country-level figure available, from the ITU (as reported via TheGlobalEconomy.com) for 2016, puts Uganda's international internet bandwidth at approximately 4 kilobits per second per internet user, within the "very low" band of under 5 kbit/s per user. No more recent country-specific bandwidth-per-user statistics have been published by ITU, the World Bank or TeleGeography. Uganda's international fibre and submarine cable capacity has expanded considerably since 2016, with the national fibre backbone growing from roughly 5,700km in 2013 to over 30,000km by 2023 and new regional submarine cable capacity added, but no updated per-user bandwidth estimate is available to confirm the current band.
